facts.fact: Mani is the turnkey at the foot of the palace cell stair, who accepts Usha's word that Neela is a new guard carrying supper.
facts.why: needed because Neela must get past a warder to reach Chathu's cell.

facts.fact: The cell stair has 104 steps; Chathu's cell is the eighth door, a rock cut three paces by four with a cot, bucket and sea slit.
facts.why: needed to place the cells under the sea cliff.

facts.fact: The sea stair rises 110 steps from the water gate, roofed against spray, to a black wooden door in a screened passage; the queen's room is the third door beyond it. A red lacquer chest with a gold bird and a farm lock sits under its window and holds the crown leaf.
facts.why: required by the beat (sea stair, queen's room, lacquer chest).

facts.fact: The queen sits audience in the long hall from the noon gun until the water-clock turns; the gun shakes the rock and covers a footstep.
facts.why: required by the beat (noon gun covers a footstep).

facts.fact: Chathu's tin of sweets was still warm in a cell with no fire; Neela notes someone warmed it and does not ask who.
facts.why: small clue that the household expected her visit; supports the saved-or-sold ambiguity.

facts.fact: The queen sent her steward on the second day with a list of the forty names with blanks, asking Chathu to write the pages fresh; he has not answered.
facts.why: required by the beat (queen asked him to write the forty again).

facts.fact: Chathu is allowed only a pot of common ink and a reed; his fingertips are stained dry grey-brown, not tacky black resin-ink (clues C03/C17).
Chathu says he wept for Ammu in the cell the first night.
facts.why: fits his bible contradiction habit (weeps when a member dies); shows pity/hate.

facts.fact: Usha promised two knocks if anyone came down the cell stair; none came before the grey-cloaked steward arrived.
facts.why: needed so the steward's arrival is a surprise and raises the question of who knew.
